'''Alexei Lvovich Efros''' ({{langx|ru|Алексей Львович Эфрос}}, born 1938) is an American [[Theoretical physicists|theoretical physicist]] who specializes in [[condensed matter physics]]. He is currently a distinguished professor at [[University of Utah]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://academic-affairs.utah.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2015/03/Distinguished-Professors-List-2016-5.pdf |title=Alexei Efros |publisher=utah.edu |access-date=February 11, 2017 |archive-date=January 12, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170112153024/http://academic-affairs.utah.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2015/03/Distinguished-Professors-List-2016-5.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Biography==
Efros was born in 1938 in [[Saint Petersburg|Leningrad]], [[Soviet Union]].<ref name=":0" />  He received his Master of Science from [[Leningrad Polytechnic Institute]] in 1961, and his PhD from the [[Ioffe Physico-Technical Institute]] in 1962. Following graduation, he continued working at the Ioffe Institute and in the process received a second PhD in 1972 in [[semiconductor]] physics. In 1986, he received the [[Landau Prize]] in theoretical physics from the [[Soviet Academy of Sciences]]. In 1987 he was promoted to principal scientist at the Ioffe Institute and served as a professor in the Leningrad Electro-Technical Institute. During the [[dissolution of the Soviet Union]] in 1989 he emigrated to the United States and was a visiting distinguished scholar at [[University of California, Riverside]]. In 1991, he moved to the [[University of Utah]] and was promoted to distinguished professor in 1994. In 1992, he was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] "for his work on the theory of transport in disordered systems". In 1997, he received the [[Humboldt Prize]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alexei L. Efros - Cirriculum Vitae|url=http://www.physics.utah.edu/~efros/vitae.html|website=University of Utah Department of Physics|access-date=12 June 2017}}</ref>

In 2018, he received the [[Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize|2019 Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Physics Prize]] for "''pioneering research in the physics of disordered materials and hopping conductivity''" together with [[Elihu Abrahams]] and [[Boris Shklovskii|Boris I. Shklovskii]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Efros&first_nm=Alexei&year=2019|title=2019 Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Physics Prize Recipient|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2018-10-23}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Efros's son, [[Alexei A. Efros]] is an associate professor of computer science at [[UC Berkeley]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alexei A. Efros homepage|url=https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~efros/|website=EECS Department|publisher=University of California, Berkeley|access-date=26 April 2017}}</ref>
